title: Provision and Wreck
premise: Riverboat captain Ada Okafor, who has spent fifteen years hiding from a past tied to the fallen Republic of Kessara, salvages a sealed chest from a shifting sandbar—inside are concession permits naming her father, the republic's disgraced surveyor, as co-holder. Hunted by a mining syndicate that wants the permits voided and by exiles who want them honored, Ada must pilot her aging boat upriver to the republic's forbidden source, where the original land grants were buried with the nation's archives. She arrives as the permits expire, and instead of claiming wealth or power, she burns them—choosing to give the river country back to the communities who never stopped living there, and finding in her ragtag crew the family her bloodline never gave her.
about_author: Coral Sterling is the pen name of a former barge-hand turned novelist who spent a decade working inland waterways before trading the wheelhouse for a writing desk. Their fiction blends river lore, political intrigue, and characters who find belonging in the most unseaworthy places.

chapters.title: What the Sandbar Keeps
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. During a low-water season run, Ada and her crew—engineer Bex and deckhand Tumo—salvage a chest stamped with the dead Republic of Kessara's seal, containing concession permits bearing her father's name. Ada's carefully invisible life cracks open as she realizes the river has been keeping her father's secret. Emotional beat: dread and reluctant curiosity; the past knocking on a door she welded shut.

chapters.title: Every Mile a Bargain
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, with a Bex interlude. A syndicate agent offers Ada a fortune to surrender the permits; that night, Kessaran exiles offer her a movement instead. Torn between selling out, joining a cause she doesn't believe in, and running, Ada learns the permits expire in forty days and the originals lie at the republic's forbidden source. Emotional beat: the corrupting pull of power offered freely, and the first flicker of loyalty to her crew over herself.

chapters.title: Upstream of the Law
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The run to the source: rapids, a syndicate gunboat on their wake, and a betrayal when Bex, tempted by the syndicate's promise to restore her revoked engineer's license, nearly sells their route. Ada forgives her—recognizing her own fifteen years of self-preservation—and they navigate the last gorge by night, running aground within sight of the drowned archive vault. Emotional beat: found family forged in damage and forgiveness; rising desperation as the deadline closes.

chapters.title: The Source Gives Nothing Back
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At the vault, Ada confronts her father's recorded confession: he falsified the grants that dispossessed the river communities. As the permits expire at dawn, the syndicate arrives; Ada burns the documents before them, voiding every claim, and lets the river take the ash. The crew, now unmistakably her family, turns the boat home. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into release—identity claimed not through inheritance, but through choice.
